title: CLIP: Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training
reading: The slide introduces CLIP, which trains an image encoder and a text encoder jointly so that the model predicts which captions go with which images in a batch. At test time this enables zero-shot, open-vocabulary classification of an image. The canonical three-panel CLIP figure from Radford et al. (ICML 2021) is reproduced beneath the bullets, and the paper is cited at the bottom.

visuals.description: Three-panel CLIP figure: (1) Contrastive pre-training, where a batch of texts goes through a Text Encoder into T1..TN and images through an Image Encoder into I1..IN, forming an N×N dot-product similarity matrix with the diagonal highlighted; (2) Create dataset classifier from label text, where class names (plane, car, dog, ... bird) are inserted into the prompt template 'A photo of a {object}.' and encoded into T1..TN; (3) Use for zero-shot prediction, where a test image is encoded to I1, compared against all Ti, and the highest similarity (I1·T3) yields 'A photo of a dog.'
visuals.assertion: Contrastive training maximizes similarity of matched image-text pairs on the diagonal and minimizes off-diagonal pairs; the same text encoder then builds a classifier from prompted label names, letting the model classify unseen images without task-specific training.

concepts.name: CLIP
concepts.why_it_matters: Foundational vision-language model linking images and text in a shared embedding space.

concepts.name: Contrastive learning
concepts.why_it_matters: Training objective that pulls matched pairs together and pushes mismatched pairs apart.

concepts.name: Zero-shot / open-vocabulary classification
concepts.why_it_matters: Allows classifying into arbitrary label sets specified in natural language at test time.

concepts.name: Prompt template
concepts.why_it_matters: 'A photo of a {object}.' converts class names into text usable by the text encoder.

verbatim_spans: Training: trains an image encoder and a text encoder to predict the correct pairings of a batch of (image, text) training examples
Testing: zero-shot, open-vocabulary classification of an image
Radford et al., Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision, ICML 2021
